transcript.text: Thank you, Alex, for sharing those constraints — that's important for getting the working arrangement right. Here are my scheduling considerations as cross-team partner: First, if corrections are moving to follow-ups or sidebars rather than being handled live in the coordination meeting, we need to build in a clear turnaround expectation — ideally within 24 to 48 hours — so that dependent partner teams aren't blocked waiting for issues to be resolved. Second, given Alex's 60 percent workload cap and 10:00 or later meeting start time, I'd recommend we schedule the main coordination meeting at 10:00 or shortly after, and designate a specific follow-up window later in the same day for sidebar corrections, so that the rhythm is predictable for all partner teams. Third, the facilitated repair meeting Nikhil recommended should be scheduled within the first week of the reset period, and its timing should also respect Alex's caregiving constraints. Finally, I'd suggest we establish a lightweight async channel for flagging correction items between meetings, so that nothing gets lost and partner teams have visibility into when their issues will be addressed. With those considerations on the table, I think we have everything needed for you to finalize the plan, Maya.
